title: RouteWorkflowRequest
description:
A route request to a routing source: the engine's request (its fields at
the top level of the JSON) plus overlay sets and mobility input.

departureAtMs.description:
When the trip departs (UTC ms): the time overlay windows are
evaluated at, unless the costing options set
`conditional_restriction_eval_at_ms`; absent both, the time of the
request.

geometryFormat.description:
How the result carries its geometry: as `points` (the default), or
encoded as `polyline6` or `geojson` wherever the result has one
(the route, each segment, leg, alternative and direct leg), with
`geometry` left empty there.

include.description:
The optional parts of the result to keep ([`RouteResultPart`]);
absent, all of them. `[]` keeps the core alone.

legDynamicOverlays.description:
Dynamic overlays (split edges, connectors) for one routed leg only,
keyed by leg index, so a leg's connectors are not exposed to the
others' endpoints.

legs.description:
How each leg is travelled, one per pair of consecutive locations;
empty: every leg is routed.

locations.description:
The origin, any waypoints in order, and the destination (2 to
[`MAX_ROUTE_LOCATIONS`]).

overlaySets.description:
Overlay sets (`crate::overlay_set`) whose live items join the
request's overlays, bound edges where a set is bound to this package,
re-projected geometry otherwise. Sets with one `setId` are merged
first.

overlays.description: Closures and other overlays, as geometry or package edges.

GeometryFormat.description: How a route result carries its geometry.

oneOf.description: `geometry`: an array of `{lat, lng}` points.
`polyline6`: an encoded polyline at precision 6; `geometry` is empty.

`geojson`: a GeoJSON `LineString` (longitude first, 6 decimals);
`geometry` is empty.
Routed and costed exactly as `Wheeled`.

A road vehicle (car, van, truck), costed close to driving time.
Private and destination-only roads only at a route's ends.

A tracked or off-road vehicle on the vehicle network: tracks are
strongly preferred, and speeds are capped (30 km/h on tracks, 42 km/h
on main roads). Private and destination-only roads only at a route's
ends.

An emergency vehicle: the roads cars may use and busways, and not
confined to through roads (it may cross private and destination-only
roads).

A person walking, costed close to walking time (about 5 km/h), as
Valhalla's pedestrian costing: footways, paths and streets alike.

Travel on foot that keeps to tracks and paths: the ways `OnFoot` may
use, and bikeable ways `foot=no` closes to it (a cycleway with
`foot=no`, a track with `access=no, bicycle=yes`). Tracks and paths cost
half as much as streets, main roads are avoided more strongly, and the
pace on tracks and paths is faster (6–6.5 km/h).

RouteEdgeSpeedOverrideRange.description:
A speed override (km/h) on a stretch of an edge
(`RouteOptions::edge_speed_override_ranges`).

RouteOffNetworkOptions.description:
Costed off-network access legs on a request (`RouteOptions::off_network`).
Every field is optional: `"offNetwork": {}` turns access legs on with the
profile's defaults.

costFactor.description:
Cost per second of access time, at least 1 and at most
[`ACCESS_MAX_COST_FACTOR`]: above 1, roads stay preferred over open
ground at the same pace. Defaults to 2 for walkers and 1.5 for
vehicles.

maxCandidates.description:
Directed candidate edges per point, 1 to [`ACCESS_MAX_CANDIDATES`]
(default [`ACCESS_DEFAULT_CANDIDATES`], or
[`ACCESS_PRICED_DEFAULT_CANDIDATES`] with a pricer). It replaces
`candidateLimit`.

maxRadiusM.description:
How far from a point to look for the road network, metres: finite,
above 0 and at most [`ACCESS_MAX_RADIUS_M`]. Defaults to
[`ACCESS_DEFAULT_RADIUS_WALKING_M`] for walkers and
[`ACCESS_DEFAULT_RADIUS_VEHICLE_M`] for vehicles. It replaces
`maxCorrelationDistanceM` and its widening.

paceMps.description:
Pace across open ground, m/s: above 0 and at most
[`ACCESS_MAX_PACE_MPS`]. Defaults to the profile's off-road pace (the
pace of direct legs).

candidateLimit.description: Correlation candidates kept per endpoint (at most 16).

edgeSpeedOverrideRanges.description:
Speed overrides on stretches of edges: the stretch takes its length
at the given speed, the rest of the edge its own time.

edgeSpeedOverrides.description:
Speed overrides (km/h) on whole edges: the edge's travel time becomes
its length at that speed, and its cost follows (cost is time times
the edge's factors). Faster than the profile's own speed is a
discount; it is costed exactly, with bounds scaled by the least
cost ratio.

maxVisitedEdgeCount.description:
Budget for one search: the most out-edges it may examine before it
stops with `SearchBudgetExceeded`. A route is one search. A matrix
applies it to each search separately, never to the request as a
whole: to each cell when cells are searched pairwise (on a package
with CCH potentials, up to 64 searchable targets on foot and any
number with a vehicle; without them, up to 12 on foot and 50 with a
vehicle), and to each source row's shared expansion above that
cut-off. Cells a stopped search had not reached fail with
`search_budget_exceeded`; targets a stopped row had already reached
keep their best path so far. Isochrones ignore it and use
`RouteIsochroneRequest::max_expansion_edge_count`.

offNetwork.description:
Costed off-network access legs (`crate::access`): every location's
candidates within the access radius are priced by a straight stretch
from the point, which results include. Off when absent.

openedEdgeIds.description:
Edges the request opens for its profile (an overlay `open`): costed
like an accessible edge of the profile even where legal access, a
destination-only rule or a conditional closure closes it. A block
still wins. Endpoints do not snap onto edges the profile cannot use.

edges.description:
Explicit edges (an overlay set bound to this package): used instead
of projecting `points`, which may then be empty.

profiles.description: The profiles the overlay applies to; empty: every profile.

speedKph.description: `discount` and `open`: the speed (km/h) on the covered edges.

validFromMs.description: The overlay is active from this time (UTC ms) on; absent: always.

validToMs.description: The overlay is active before this time (UTC ms); absent: always.

RouteOverlayGeometryKind.description: The shape of an overlay's geometry.

RouteOverlayPolicy.description:
What an overlay does to the edges it covers.
Inside one request: a block wins over a discount and a slow-go; an
`open` wins over legal closure and over a block whose `valid_from_ms` is
earlier than its own (an absent one is earliest); overlapping discounts
multiply, slow-go factors take the largest, and of several speed
overrides on one edge the slowest stands.

oneOf.description: Blocked.
Dearer: `cost_multiplier` above 1 (default 2), cost only.
A hazard warning on the route; costs are unchanged.

Usable by the request's profile (when `profiles` lists it, or lists
none) whatever its legal access says, at `speed_kph` if given. The
edge must be in the package; endpoints do not snap onto it.

package.description: The package the items' `edges` are bound to.

author.description: Who wrote the item; a merge fills it from the item's set.

edges.description: Edge ids of the bound package (`RouteOverlaySet::package`).

profiles.description: The profiles the item applies to; empty: every profile.

oneOf.description: No-go.
Slow-go: a cost multiplier above 1.
A hazard warning.
Cheaper: a multiplier in (0, 1) or a speed override.
Usable for the listed profiles whatever their legal access.

RouteOverlaySource.description: Where an overlay came from, when it came from an overlay set.

RouteResultPart.description: An optional part of a route result, named in a request's `include`.

oneOf.description:
`segments`: each leg's full single-leg result. Left out, `segments`
is empty and `segmentSummaries` has each leg's distance, duration and
cost.

The `legs` of each segment and alternative: their geometry, edges
and shape segments split at waypoints.
`edgeAttributions`, and every leg's `edges`.
The `costBreakdown` of every edge attribution that is kept.
`shapeSegments`, and every leg's `shapeSegments`.
`recosts`, and each segment's.

RouteSarOptions.description:
The SAR option of a request (`RouteOptions::sar`). An absent relaxation
is not relaxed. JSON names are snake_case with camelCase aliases.

RouteSarRelaxations.description: The relaxations of a SAR request, each absent unless named.

RouteWorkflowMobilityInput.description:
Portable, precompiled mobility influence.

Loading patches and sampling an elevation source are deliberately outside
the route kernel. The hybrid-routing compiler turns those artifacts into
these edge/range adjustments and an optional dynamic overlay; therefore DEM
slope still changes route costs without giving this service package paths,
raster formats, or renderer imagery.

legDynamicOverlays.description:
Connector overlays keyed by their stable workflow leg index. These are
merged only for the corresponding routed leg, preventing endpoint nodes
from exposing another leg's origin/destination connectors.

elevationModelVersion.description: Identifies the elevation/cost model already folded into range costs.

SarConditional.description: R6: `ignore` (default true when the relaxation is named).

SarLegalAccess.description:
R1. `military` is relaxed only when listed; `private` or `customers`
lift the destination-only confinement of the whole request (see
`lifts_destination_only`).

SarMotorBlocking.description: How R4 treats barriers that block motor vehicles (bollards, blocks).

oneOf.description: Impassable for vehicles (the default).
Passable on foot only: the route ends its vehicle part there.

costed.description:
X6: cost the leg (`crate::access`, at the profile's off-road pace and
a cost factor of 1). The join is then chosen by total time among the
candidates within `max_leg_m`, and the route's cost, duration,
distance, geometry and maneuvers include the leg; the report's
`added_cost_s` is both the cost and the duration they add. Off by
default: the leg is reported and left out of the totals.

SarTurnRestrictions.description: R3: each violated simple or complex restriction costs `penalty_s`.

SarUnknownWidth.description: Whether R5 admits paths of unknown width.
